Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - notes & next steps

Hi Matt & Karen,

Thanks again for the call today - great to learn more about PaymentSys' planned rollout. Quick recap and proposed next steps to lock in Dedicated capacity sizing: 

Key items from our call:
- Target geos: US (primary), possibility to expand to EU in Q4.
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + post-chat generation (short prompts) and periodic batch reranking for fraud signals.
- TPS targets: steady-state ~25 TPS, expected peak bursts to ~120 TPS during promotions.
- Concurrency: typical per-request concurrency target 8 concurrent streams; long-running sessions for chat up to 100 concurrent active users.
- Token mix: average request ~120 prompt tokens, average response ~300 tokens; heavier batch jobs up to 5k tokens.
- Desired SLA: 99.9% p95 latency <= 200ms for short gen.
- Security: VPC + SOC2 required; procurement will ask for evidence.

Questions we still have (can you confirm?):
1) Are the 120 TPS bursts expected to be sustained for more than ~10 minutes?
2) Any model preferences? You mentioned staying on a 13B variant vs larger models for cost reasons.
3) Will batch reranking run on a schedule (nightly) or ad-hoc during business hours?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) and Rafael (SE lead) to propose a sizing recommendation (GPU type, pool counts, burst config) and a draft pricing envelope.
- Please fill the attached sizing template with any additional traffic patterns you have.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

Thanks,

Marissa / Aditya / Matt -

Quick sizing options based on the supplied profile. Assumptions: 13B quantized model (8-bit), avg request 420 tokens total, steady 25 TPS, peak bursts 120 TPS for ~30 minutes, batch reranks nightly (offpeak).

Option A (cost-efficient):
- GPU: A10G (good price/perf for 13B quantized).
- Pool: 3 pods (each pod = 2x A10G), steady capacity handles ~30 TPS comfortably with autoscale headroom; burst leverages pre-warmed extra pod to handle spikes up to ~90 TPS; for 120 TPS need 1-2 minutes of scale-up.
- Expected p95 latency for short gen: ~220-350ms depending on concurrency.
- Notes: Best unit cost; may not meet strict 200ms p95 SLA in worst-case burst.

Option B (balanced latency):
- GPU: A100 40GB (fp16 optimized).
- Pool: 2 pods (each pod = 1x A100), steady capacity handles 25 TPS with comfortable concurrency; burst capacity up to 160 TPS with fast autoscale and cache reuse.
- Expected p95 latency: ~120-180ms for short gen.
- Notes: Higher cost but meets target SLA reliably.

Option C (high-SLA / low-latency):
- GPU: H100 or 80GB A100s depending on availability.
- Pool: 2-3 pods (1x H100 each), pre-provisioned burst reserve; no cold-starts for peak windows.
- Expected p95 latency: ~80-150ms.
- Notes: Premium cost; recommended if strict latency SLAs are required.

Other recommendations:
- Configure prefix KV caching for common prompts to reduce token work on hot paths.
- Use burst policy with short warm-up (30-90s) + fallback to Hosted API for rare >peak events.
- Enable KMS integration and share SOC2 artifacts (I'll attach SOC2 pointer for procurement).

I attached a short sizing worksheet and a draft proposal (pricing envelope) for PS-4257. Happy to hop on a quick call with your infra folks to finalize.

Attachments: proposal-PS-4257-v1.pdf, redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx
